### Introduction to GPU Memory Hierarchy

Unlike CPUs, which rely on a relatively simple hierarchy of registers, L1/L2/L3 caches, and main RAM, GPUs (Graphics Processing Units) utilize a complex, multi-level memory hierarchy designed to maximize throughput for massively parallel workloads. The goal of this hierarchy is to keep the thousands of cores in a GPU fed with data as quickly as possible, minimizing the time spent waiting for data from slower, off-chip memory.

The hierarchy is generally organized from fastest/smallest (closest to the compute cores) to slowest/largest (off-chip).
